_doc: Fundo 'imagem alinhada ao céu' (2026-10-19; resolve.hlsl backgroundAt mode 2): how each painted backdrop sits against the real sky. Rows are shares of the painting's height (0 top .. 1 bottom): horizon = the painting's own horizon row, pinned to the world's horizon; bottom = the last row kept (1 = the whole painting, the user's choice: 'use the whole image and just add atmosphere and sky on the top layer'; less cuts the ground away and fades it into the sky's horizon colour); skyTop = above this row the painting is always sky (matted out; between skyTop and horizon the painting's sky is found by colour against its top rows). degreesPerHeight = the elevation the painting's whole height would span above the horizon (its vertical scale there); bottomDegrees = the scale of the rows just below the horizon (a cut painting: how far down its `bottom` row lands; a painting kept whole: its last row lands at the nadir, the ground compressing smoothly towards it, one continuous image at any tilt). spanDegrees = the azimuth the painting's width spans (mirrored beyond its edges); glowColumn = the column of the painting's own sun glow (0 left .. 1 right), turned to sit under the real sun; horizonDegrees = the elevation (degrees, negative = below the real horizon) where the painting's horizon row sits (the user: 'o cenário está muito alto'; the real sky reaches down to the painting's ridge). ground = the map's top-down ground image around the board (content/backdrops, cooked into the ground pack; the user's AldeiaGround for aldeia), groundTile = its width in world units (mirrored at its edges), groundFar = the distance along the view ray beyond which the painting takes over (the horizon band). 'default' serves paintings not listed.
